title: Seed pages and their owners
bridge: Drafting a seed page is like opening a draft PR from an AI suggestion. The draft is useful, but a person must review it before it ships. Except: here the "review" is a frontmatter field, confidence, and only the page owner may raise it to high.
intro: A brain with 35 small pages that people ask about beats a dump of 300. This lesson shows how we pick those pages from real demand, draft them with Claude Code, and get owners to check them. Owners raise confidence only after reading the code, so agents know which pages they can trust.

picture.caption: Every page starts as an AI draft at confidence: low and ends as an owner-checked page at med or high.

nodes.label: Claude Code in an fcp checkout

steps.text: picks pages from real questions; each has an owner who said yes and 2 to 5 sources
gives it one entry: the sources and templates/page.md
writes a one-screen page that cites its sources
checks claims against the sources, runs kb lint and kb index
opens one PR per owner with a few pages
fixes what is wrong, sets reviewed and raises confidence honestly

p: The first question is not "what do we know?" but "what do people ask?". Shai collects demand from three places, listed below. Private channels count only as summaries.
First, questions in public engineering channels over the last six months. Second, onboarding gaps from the last two hires. Third, the topics the BE guild skills explain most.

The target is about 18 engineering, 6 product, 6 decision (ADR) and 5 runbook pages. Cross-team topics come first: cloud and client, CI, QA environments, releases. One person's knowledge blocks others there.
Each entry needs an owner who agreed on Slack before drafting starts, and 2 to 5 sources. The plan is one YAML file in rnd-kb, deleted once the pages exist.
sections.because: We write the plan as data because the drafting step reads it entry by entry. The owners can also review the list before any page is written.

code.text:
# rnd-kb/seed-plan.yml: the seed list; deleted once the pages exist (G6-15)
# Each entry: where the page goes, who owns it, what the AI draft must read. Sources follow DATA-SCOPE.md.
pages:
  - path: engineering/code-run-path.md
    title: How a code run reaches the on-prem client
    owner: "@RhinoHealth/backend-guild"
    sources:
      - https://github.com/RhinoHealth/fcp/tree/main/common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc
      - https://github.com/RhinoHealth/fcp/tree/main/client/rhinoOnPrem/rhinoAgentRpc/handlers
    demand: "<permalink to a public thread, or 'onboarding gap'>"
  - path: engineering/ci-map.md
    title: Which CI workflow runs what, and when
    owner: "@RhinoHealth/devops"
    sources:
      - https://github.com/RhinoHealth/fcp/tree/main/.github/workflows # cloud/client/sdk CI on push, frontend CI on pull_request
    demand: "<permalink>"
  - path: runbooks/integration-test-lock.md
    title: What to do when integration tests wait for the QA lock
    owner: "@RhinoHealth/devops"
    sources:
      - https://github.com/RhinoHealth/fcp/blob/main/.github/workflows/_cloud-int-tests-reusable-aws.yml # one lock per component per cloud
    demand: "<permalink>"
  # ... 32 more; owners confirmed in Slack before drafting

notes.text: The file is temporary. G6-15 deletes it when 30 pages pass lint at med or high.
pages: a list; each entry becomes one page.
path: where the page goes, relative to the rnd-kb root. The folder sets the kind of page.
title: the same title that will go into the frontmatter.
owner: an entry from OWNERS.yml. Quoted, because @ starts a YAML tag otherwise.
sources: what the AI draft must read. These become the page's sources field.
demand: the public thread that asked, or the words 'onboarding gap'. It proves the page is wanted.
A runbook entry. Runbooks answer 'what do I do when it is red', so the source is the workflow that holds the lock.
32 more entries follow; owners are confirmed in Slack before drafting.

sections.h: Draft the engineering pages with Claude Code (G6-07)
p: For each entry Shai runs Claude Code in an fcp checkout with rnd-kb added: claude --add-dir ../rnd-kb. The prompt gives the sources and templates/page.md and asks for a short page. It has a one-paragraph summary and the path step by step. Then why it is built this way, what breaks if you change it, and where to look first.

Then the human step: check every claim against the sources. A claim with no source is deleted, not softened. The frontmatter gets owner, reviewed (today), review_every 90d, confidence low, sources and applies_to. Then kb lint and kb index.
You saw the frontmatter of this page in g6-1. Here is the body.
sections.because: We fix the section order for every engineering page. A reader who knows the shape finds the answer faster, and the bot can quote the right section.

code.text:
# How a code run reaches the on-prem client

**In short.** The client runs inside the customer's network and opens the connection to the cloud; the cloud never
connects in. Work for the client travels back over that reverse gRPC stream, and the client's handlers run it next to
the customer's data.

## Step by step
1. <each step names the file that does it, checked against the sources>

## Why it is built this way
Customer networks don't accept inbound connections, and patient data stays on the customer's side.

## What breaks if you change it
- The protos in `common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/` are a contract with clients already installed at customers.
  Add fields; don't rename or remove them. Regenerate with `make protoc` and commit the _pb2 files.

## Where to look first
`client/rhinoOnPrem/rhinoAgentRpc/handlers/`, `cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoAgentRpc/`

notes.text: The H1 repeats the title. One page, one topic.
In short: one paragraph a newcomer can act on. It names the one fact that matters: the client dials out.
Step by step: a numbered list where each step names the file that does it. The draft leaves a placeholder; the owner fills it from the sources.
Why it is built this way: the reason the code cannot show.
What breaks if you change it: the contract with installed clients. This is what an agent must read before editing a proto.
The concrete rule: add fields, never rename or remove; regenerate with make protoc; commit the _pb2 files.
Where to look first: two paths. Link code by path; never paste code into a page.

callout.text: One PR per owner, a few pages each. The reviewer is the page owner, not Shai. An owner who reviews only their own three pages reads them properly.

p: Product pages explain what each product area does for the user, with the Jira epic and the Drive doc as sources. From private channels only summaries, and never a customer name: write "a customer".

Decision pages are ADRs: architecture decision records. Each has a status, the context, the decision and its consequences. We start with ADR-0001 (the brain home) and this quarter's agent-platform choices. One fresh VM per run, and Temporal orchestrates. The broker and gateway hold the keys, and the platform is TypeScript on Node 24 like Byte.
Runbooks: integration tests waiting for the QA lock, main is red, Byte failed on my PR, FCP Lab won't start. Every step in a runbook is a command or a link.
sections.because: We give ADRs a status field because a superseded decision must still be readable. It points to the one that replaced it.

code.text:
---
title: "ADR-0002: Each agent run gets its own fresh VM"
owner: "@RhinoHealth/devops" # decide: an owner for agent-platform ADRs (there is no Platform team on GitHub yet)
reviewed: 2026-10-27
review_every: 180d
confidence: low
status: accepted
sources:
  - RH-9214
applies_to: []
---

notes.text: ADR titles carry their number, so a page can cite ADR-0002 by name.
Owner: DevOps for now. There is no Platform team on GitHub yet, so this is a decision to make.
Decisions change slowly, so review_every is 180d.
status is the field only decisions/ pages have (schema.py allows proposed, accepted, superseded).
The source is the Jira epic for the agent runtime, RH-9214.
applies_to is empty: a decision is not about one code path.

sections.h: The body of a decision record
p: The body has three fixed headings. Context says what was true when we decided. Decision says what we chose, in plain words with the numbers. Consequences lists what follows, good and bad, so a reader later knows what the decision cost.
sections.because: We keep the three ADR headings fixed. The bot and the ingest routine look for them when they answer "why is it like this?".

code.text:
# ADR-0002: Each agent run gets its own fresh VM

## Context
Agents read untrusted input (tickets, code, web pages) and need Docker for FCP Lab. Anthropic's hosted and
self-hosted agent environments are not available to ZDR organizations.

## Decision
Every run (a Nova ticket, a bug fix, a CI fix) gets a new EC2 VM in the ai-agents AWS account, in one of three
sizes (lite, full, wide), taken from a warm pool and destroyed when the run ends. A VM waiting on a person is
stopped, and after 72 hours destroyed with its work saved.

## Consequences
- Nothing from one run (a process, a file, a cached secret) can reach the next one.
- A run starts in about a minute from the warm pool; stopped VMs cost only their disk.
- Firecracker microVMs are a Q1 test.

notes.text: The H1 repeats the ADR title.
Context: agents read untrusted input and need Docker, and Anthropic's hosted environments are not available to ZDR organizations.
Decision: a fresh EC2 VM per run, three sizes, from a warm pool, destroyed at the end. A VM waiting on a person stops, and after 72 hours is destroyed with its work saved.
Consequences, good: nothing leaks from one run to the next.
Consequences, cost: a VM starts in about a minute; stopped VMs cost only their disk.
An open follow-up belongs here too: Firecracker microVMs are a Q1 test.

sections.h: Owners check and raise confidence (G6-11, G6-15)
p: AI drafts are leads, not facts. Shai posts each owner's PR in Slack with a short ask: read, fix, set confidence honestly. high means checked against main this week. med means mostly right with one part unchecked. Owners edit in the PR, set reviewed to the review date, and delete claims they cannot confirm.

Anything an owner says is missing becomes a line in an existing page or a short new page. Never a big new page. The bar for G6-11 is at least 15 of the 18 engineering pages at med or high by the end of W6.

G6-15 repeats the flow for the product, decision and runbook pages, and Shai writes the gap pages owners asked for. Then seed-plan.yml is deleted and index.md is shared in a public engineering channel. That happens when kb lint on main shows at least 30 pages at med or high.
sections.because: We show the owner's change as a diff, because that is all an owner review changes in the frontmatter. Two dates, one confidence, maybe a source.

code.text:
---
 title: How a code run reaches the on-prem client
 owner: "@RhinoHealth/backend-guild"
-reviewed: 2026-10-20
+reviewed: 2026-11-03
 review_every: 90d
-confidence: low # AI draft from the sources below; the owner raises it after checking
+confidence: high # checked against main by the owner

   - https://github.com/RhinoHealth/fcp/tree/main/common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc
+  - RH-6812

notes.text: reviewed moves from the draft date to the day the owner checked the page.
The owner's date, two weeks later.
low with the draft comment goes away.
high, with a comment that says why: checked against main by the owner. Only an owner may write high.
The owner adds a source they used: a Jira key. More sources make the next review faster.

callout.text: Why 30 pages? That is the bar for Nova and Byte to read the brain through the kb skill (g6-4). And BRAIN-QA (g6-5) needs real, checked source pages to score against.

quiz.q: Shai drafts a page with Claude Code. One claim has no source. What happens to it?

options.text: It stays, with 'probably' added in front.
options.why: Softening a claim still leaves a claim the bot will repeat. The rule is delete, not soften.

options.text: It is deleted before the PR is opened.
options.why: G6-07: delete a claim with no source instead of softening it.

options.text: It stays at confidence: low and the owner decides.
options.why: The owner reviews facts with sources; an unsourced claim wastes their review.

quiz.q: Who may set confidence: high on a page?

options.why: Shai drafts at low; high means a person checked the page against main.

options.text: The page owner, after checking it against main this week.
options.why: That is the definition of high in G6-11, and the owner is the PR reviewer.

options.text: The ingest routine, when the page cites a merged PR.
options.why: The routine (g6-5) never sets confidence above med.

quiz.q: A product page draws on a private Slack thread that names a customer. What goes in the page?

options.text: A quote of the thread with the customer name, since the source is cited.
options.why: Private channels are summaries only, and customer names never go in (DATA-SCOPE.md).

options.text: A summary in our own words that says 'a customer'.
options.why: That follows DATA-SCOPE.md: summaries from private channels, no customer names.

options.text: Nothing; private threads cannot be used at all.
options.why: They can be used as summaries; only verbatim quotes are out.

An AI draft that no person has checked yet; readers and the bot treat it as a lead, not a fact.
The person or GitHub team in the owner field; the only one who may raise confidence to high.
